_note: The Modern Mirror: what each part of Atlantis is in the real world. 'rooms' shows in each building; 'topics' are the lessons a season report can pick (app/engine/report.py chooses which).

bank.text: Everyday money. Earns almost nothing; a stolen debit card drains it.
Earns interest, and the FDIC insures it up to $250,000. Often grows slower than prices.
30% a year. US card rates average over 20%, so carried balances snowball.
300 to 850, like FICO. Paying on time is 35% of it.
A deposit becomes your limit: how people with no history start building credit.

market.text: The bill you can't skip. Bird flu doubled US egg prices in 2022.
Pays nothing, but has held its value for centuries.
Big orders move prices. That's why big funds buy slowly.

harbor.text: Where you buy shares: small pieces of companies.
Steady, and pays you part of its profit. Coca-Cola has raised its dividend 60+ years running.
Can double in a year, or halve.
A rare jackpot, and a loss on average.
500 big companies in one buy, so one bad year barely dents it.
Stocks fell 57% in 2007–09. Those forced to sell, sold at the bottom.
Paid in cash on the day. Paper wealth doesn't count until it's sold.

guild_hall.text: Reliable and slow. Big goals usually get pricier faster than pay rises.
An hour spent one way can't be spent another: opportunity cost.
Saving wages rarely outruns rising prices. Money that earns money closes the gap.

drowned_bell.text: Built to pay back less than they take. Lotteries return about 50–65¢ per $1.
Pays back 88¢ per $1, like many slots. Rare big wins keep you playing.
GameStop went from $20 to $400 on hype in 2021, then crashed.

black_reef.text: $15 per $100 for two weeks: nearly 400% a year. Most borrowers roll it over.
The easy yes is the trap: they profit when you can't repay.

circle.text: Tandas, susus, chit funds, hui: neighbours pooling money, used worldwide.
Trust instead of interest. Some US nonprofits report the payments to build credit.

council.text: Sets interest rates and aims for 2% inflation a year.
Due every year, whatever you earned.
Rome thinned its silver coins; US prices rose 9.1% in 2022. Cash buys less.

payday_loan.name: Payday loans
payday_loan.text: Grin is a payday lender: about 400% a year. The costliest money there is.

ponzi.name: Ponzi schemes
ponzi.text: Early 'returns' are paid with later investors' money. Madoff's ran for decades. Guaranteed high returns are the tell.

missed_payment.name: Payment history
missed_payment.text: 35% of a credit score. One 30-day late payment stays on your report for 7 years.

card_interest.name: Credit card interest
card_interest.text: Interest on interest. At 20%+ a year, minimum payments can stretch a small balance over years.

card_fraud.name: Disputing charges
card_fraud.text: You have 60 days to dispute a card charge in the US. Check your statements.

house_edge.name: The house edge
house_edge.text: Every casino game pays back less than it takes. You can win a night, not a year.

cash_theft.name: Keeping cash safe
cash_theft.text: Stolen cash is gone. Bank deposits are FDIC-insured up to $250,000.

inflation.name: Inflation
inflation.text: Prices jumped; your coin didn't. In 2022 US prices rose 9.1%. Cash melts, assets tend to rise.

emergency_fund.name: Emergency funds
emergency_fund.text: 1 in 3 US adults can't cover a $400 surprise in cash. Aim for 3–6 months saved.

lottery.name: Lottery stocks
lottery.text: Like penny stocks: people overpay for a small shot at a jackpot.

index_fund.name: Index funds
index_fund.text: Like an S&P 500 fund: many companies in one buy. Real ones charge 0.03% a year.

diversify.name: Diversification
diversify.text: Enron workers lost their jobs and their savings at once, because both were in Enron.

dividends.name: Dividends
dividends.text: Profit paid to shareholders. Reinvested, they're a big part of stock returns.

rosca.name: Lending circles
rosca.text: Millions use ROSCAs to save and borrow without a bank.

seasonal_prices.name: Buying ahead
seasonal_prices.text: Buying food in season or in bulk is the simplest way to stretch a budget.

opportunity_cost.name: Opportunity cost
opportunity_cost.text: An idle tide costs the shift you didn't work.

credit_score.name: Credit scores
credit_score.text: On-time payments first, then using under 30% of your limit, then time.

savings_rate.name: Savings vs inflation
savings_rate.text: In the 2010s US savings paid under 0.1% while prices rose 2% a year.

news_shock.name: News moves markets
news_shock.text: One stuck ship in the Suez Canal (2021) froze billions in trade a day.

real_return.name: Real returns
real_return.text: Earn 5% while prices rise 3%, and you're only 2% richer.
